source_text: XIV. μισόκαλός γε μὴν ἐς τὰ μάλιστα καὶ φιλοπόνηρος ὢν ὁ τῆς ἐκκλησίας τοῦ θεοῦ πολέμιος, μηδένα τε μηδαμῶς τῆς κατὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπολιπὼν ἐπιβουλῆς τρόπον, αἱρέσεις ξένας αὖθις ἐπιφύεσθαι κατὰ τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἐνήργει· ὧν οἱ μὲν ἰοβόλων δίκην ἑρπετῶν ἐπὶ τῆς Ἀσίας καὶ Φρυγίας εἷρπον, τὸν μὲν δὴ παράκλητον Μοντανόν, τὰς δ’ ἐξ αὐτοῦ γυναῖκας, Πρίσκιλλαν καὶ Μαξίμιλλαν, ὡς ἂν τοῦ Μοντανοῦ προφήτιδας γεγονυίας, αὐχοῦντες·
pass_a_gloss: For being hateful of beauty and being hardworking, the enemy of the church of God, leaving no method of plotting against men in any way, was bringing it about that foreign heresies were again growing against the church; of which some, like poisonous snakes, were crawling in Asia and Phrygia, the so-called advocate Montanus, and the women from him, Priscilla and Maximilla, boasting, as if they had become prophetesses of Montanus

choices.term: ὁ τῆς ἐκκλησίας τοῦ θεοῦ πολέμιος
choices.english: the enemy of the church of God

choices.why: capture the specific noun 'παράκλητον' used as a title/designation

choices.term: μηδένα τε μηδαμῶς τῆς κατὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπολιπὼν ἐπιβουλῆς τρόπον
choices.english: leaving no method of plotting against men in any way

choices.term: ὡς ἂν τοῦ Μοντανοῦ προφήτιδας γεγονυίας
choices.english: as if they had become prophetesses of Montanus

pass_b_english: For the enemy of the church of God, being hateful of beauty and hardworking, and leaving no method of plotting against men in any way, was bringing it about that foreign heresies were again growing up against the church. Among these, some were crawling through Asia and Phrygia like poisonous snakes — Montanus, the so-called Advocate, and the women from him, Priscilla and Maximilla, boasting as if they had become prophetesses of Montanus.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B both correctly render the complex structure of the first sentence and the specific descriptions of Montanus and the women. The term 'παράκλητον' is correctly rendered as 'advocate' (or 'the so-called Advocate' in B to reflect the context of the Greek 'δὴ'). The description of the women as 'prophetesses' (προφήτιδας) and the comparison to 'poisonous snakes' (ἰοβόλων) are preserved.
